title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Section 6 starts a canonical 'complex-analytic realization' of a single face (a combinatorial polygon). It serves the Teichmüller/dessins programme of the surrounding pages: giving a combinatorial map a canonical Riemann-surface structure by assigning each face a canonical Riemann sphere (a hemisphere with a centre) and gluing.

(44) P = (S, A, R ⊂ S×A) is a finite combinatorial polygon of order n ≥ 3. S is the set of vertices, A the set of edges, R the incidence relation.

(45)-(46) D = Aut(P) is dihedral of order 2n. D^+ is the cyclic subgroup of index 2 of rotations, giving the extension 1 → D^+ → D → {±1} → 1.

(47) The two-element set of orientations of P is identified with the two privileged generators {ω, ω'} = {ω, ω^{-1}} of D^+. These are the one-step rotations: ω(s) is a vertex adjacent to s, and ωa is an edge adjacent to a.

(48) Claim: there is a complex projective line Σ_P, unique up to unique isomorphism, with a D-equivariant embedding S ↪ Σ_P such that D acts by holomorphic automorphisms.
- The reflections of P then act as half-turns of the sphere. They are holomorphic, not antiholomorphic.
- Uniqueness already follows from requiring only that D^+ extend. The extension of all of D is then automatic by transport of structure: uniqueness up to unique isomorphism makes any automorphism of P act on Σ_P.
- P is then realized canonically by points of Σ and arcs of great circles, all lying on one great circle, which they subdivide cellularly.

The next page continues:
- That circle defines a canonical real structure Σ_R.
- There is a unique D-invariant homogeneous metric.
- The two open hemispheres correspond to the two orientations ('Stokes correspondence', (49)).
- Σ^D = Σ^{D^+} = Σ^{ω} consists of 2 points P_ω, one in each hemisphere. P_ω is characterized by ω acting on the tangent space there as rotation by +2π/n.
- Named points: R_s for vertices, Q_a for edge midpoints.

The margin note seems to sketch the proof: take Σ^0 = P^1_C with the standard dihedral action, R ⊂ C, the real circle P^1(R), the action of SO(...), and a functor P ↦ Σ.

Modern reading: Σ_P is the Riemann sphere with D_n ⊂ PSL_2(C) ≅ SO(3)-type action. The polygon is the regular n-gon on the equator, and the two poles are the face 'centres'. Gluing such hemispheres over the faces of a map gives the canonical conformal structure on the surface of a dessin/map.
errors: Uniqueness as literally stated fails for n ≥ 5 (more precisely when φ(n) > 2, e.g. n = 5, 7, 8, ...). One can let ω act on P^1 by rotation of angle 2πk/n with k coprime to n, k ≠ ±1. An equivariant embedding of S still exists (the vertices then form a 'star polygon'). It is not D-equivariantly isomorphic to the standard one, since conjugation preserves the rotation angle at the fixed points. An extra normalization is needed: ω must act at P_ω by angle ±2π/n, or equivalently adjacent vertices must bound arcs forming a cellular subdivision of the circle. The next page states this angle condition as a characterization, not as a hypothesis. For n = 3, 4, 6 the statement is correct as written.

Minor subtlety, not an error. For n odd the centralizer of D_n in PGL_2(C) is not trivial: it contains the half-turn about the polar axis, and D_n × Z/2 ≅ D_{2n}. So uniqueness up to unique isomorphism holds only because the embedding of S is part of the data. This is consistent with Grothendieck's formulation, but the margin proof would need it.

ideas.what: Orientations of a polygon identified with the two generating one-step rotations of D^+, and the dihedral extension 1→D^+→D→{±1}→1
ideas.modern_name: orientation torsor of a cyclic/dihedral structure

ideas.what: Canonical Riemann sphere Σ_P attached to a combinatorial polygon, unique up to unique isomorphism, with holomorphic dihedral action extending the action on vertices
ideas.modern_name: regular n-gon on the equator of the Riemann sphere / dihedral subgroup of PSL_2(C); face-sphere in the canonical conformal structure of a map
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, finite subgroups of PSL_2(C)); its use for maps: Grothendieck (Esquisse), Jones–Singerman, Shabat–Voevodsky
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §3 sketches canonical conformal structures on map surfaces; this specific functorial formulation is not known to be published

ideas.what: Uniqueness from D^+ alone implies extension of the D-action, by transport of structure
ideas.modern_name: rigidity / functoriality via uniqueness up to unique isomorphism

ideas.what: Canonical real structure, invariant metric, hemispheres ↔ orientations, fixed points P_ω as face centres (continued on next page)
ideas.modern_name: real structure on P^1 / hemisphere decomposition used in Belyi / dessin uniformization

missed.claim: A careful functorial ('unique up to unique isomorphism') treatment of the canonical sphere of a face. It is apparently meant for building the canonical Riemann surface of a map by gluing, in Grothendieck's own hand. The construction itself is standard; only the archival detail of his functorial setup is new.
missed.quote: Il existe une droite projective complexe, unique à isomorphisme unique près, Σ=Σ_P ... l'unicité est déjà garantie en exigeant le prolongement des opérations de D^+
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's approach to the canonical conformal structure of dessins (cf. Esquisse §3). It is of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical (the regular polygon on the Riemann sphere with a dihedral action). The only interest is archival: the functorial formulation within the Teichmüller/dessins notes. There is also a minor imprecision in the uniqueness claim for n ≥ 5.
transcription_corrections: The formula label read as '(46)' looks like '(4S)' / '(45)' in the image; it is presumably (46), since (45) is already used.
Line 3: '$D_P^+=D^+$' is written over a correction ('B_p^+ = D^+'), which is consistent with the transcription.
The struck words after 'générateurs privilégiés de D^+,' read roughly 'conditions [?] ... qui [?] automorphismes'. They are deleted and not mathematically relevant.
'à tous placés sur un même (grand) cercle' is more likely '& tous placés ...' (with a struck 'derniers' before 'placés'). The intended sense is 'all lying on one same great circle'.

Margin: the formula transcribed as '$D_P^+\simeq D_P$' is uncertain. The margin also seems to contain 'Σ^0 = P^1_C', 'Σ_P', 'P(R) ⊂ P(C)', 'iso. canonique', and 'l'action des points', but it is largely illegible.
